name: Hwa-Rang
meaning: Named after the Hwa-Rang, the elite youth group of the Silla Dynasty (about 600 AD). The 29 movements refer to the 29th Infantry Division, where Tae Kwon-Do was developed.
endingPosition: Bring the right foot back to a ready posture
diagram: Floor diagram image (hwa_rang.jpg) with points A to F; no text description on the page.

movements.technique: Middle push block with left palm
Upward punch with left fist, right fist in front of left shoulder

movements.footwork: Pull left foot to right foot
movements.technique: Left palm brought to right fore-fist, right elbow bent about 45 degrees outward
Middle side piercing kick with right foot, hands pulled apart, then middle outward strike with right knife-hand

movements.footwork: Left foot to E, turning counter-clockwise

movements.technique: Middle thrust with right straight fingertip

movements.footwork: Right foot kicks, then lowers to F
movements.technique: High turning kick with right foot

movements.footwork: Left foot kicks, lowers to F (18 and 19 performed quickly)
movements.technique: High turning kick with left foot, then middle guarding knife-hand block
Side elbow thrust with right elbow

movements.footwork: Left foot to right foot, turning counter-clockwise
movements.technique: Side front block with right inner forearm, left forearm extended down to the side
Side front block with left inner forearm, right forearm extended down to the side

movements.footwork: Left foot to right foot, then right foot to A

notes: Source has a typo ('let foot') in movement 4; read as left foot.
Fetched text was paraphrased by the fetcher; footwork for several steps (stay/slide) is inferred from the step wording.
